adaptive.title: Adaptive TDEE
adaptive.building: Building up data: {available} / {required} days with both weight + diary
adaptive.until_ready: Until ready, your fixed goal of {value} {unit} applies.
adaptive.help_intro: Adaptive TDEE learns your true daily energy expenditure from your weight trend over the last 35 days, paired with how much you actually ate. The math:
adaptive.help_step_1: Smooth your weight series (linear regression over 35 days).
adaptive.help_step_2: Convert the trend into daily energy balance (1 kg of body mass ≈ 7,700 kcal).
adaptive.help_step_3: TDEE = average daily intake − that daily balance.
adaptive.help_best_weigh: Weigh yourself frequently — daily is best, every other day is fine. Sparse weights are interpolated, but more measurements = tighter signal. A connected scale (Withings, Fitbit, Garmin, Health Connect) is automatic; manual body-stats entries also work.
adaptive.help_best_log: Log your food consistently. Missing days are dropped from the calculation. The estimate gets noisy if you log half your days.
adaptive.help_best_switch: Don't switch goals mid-window. The 35-day rolling average converges over time. If you bounce between cuts and bulks weekly, the learned TDEE will lag.
adaptive.help_best_reweigh: Re-weigh in similar conditions — first thing in the morning, after using the bathroom, before food/drink. Day-to-day fluctuations are mostly water; the trend is what matters.
adaptive.help_caveats: Caveats. Big changes in activity (started running, broke a leg) take ~2 weeks to fully reflect. Travel weeks with under-logged food can pull the estimate up. The learned TDEE is multiplied by your goal factor (Lose -20% / Maintain / Gain +20%) to get your actual daily target.

wellness_metric_help.floors: Floors climbed based on elevation gain detected by your device.
wellness_metric_help.active_minutes: Time spent at a moderate or higher activity level.
wellness_metric_help.calories_out: Total calories burned including your resting metabolic rate.
wellness_metric_help.active_zone_minutes: Minutes spent in Fat Burn, Cardio, or Peak heart rate zones — counts double for Cardio and Peak.
wellness_metric_help.moderate_intensity_min: Time at moderate intensity (brisk walking, light cycling). WHO recommends 150–300 min/week.
wellness_metric_help.vigorous_intensity_min: Time at high intensity (running, hard effort). Counts double toward weekly activity targets.
wellness_metric_help.sleep_duration_min: Total time asleep last night. Adults generally need 7–9 hours.
wellness_metric_help.sleep_deep_min: Deep (slow-wave) sleep — the most restorative stage. Critical for physical recovery and immune function.
wellness_metric_help.sleep_light_min: Light sleep is the transition between wakefulness and deeper stages. Makes up the majority of most sleep cycles.
wellness_metric_help.sleep_rem_min: REM sleep supports memory consolidation, learning, and emotional regulation. Increases in later sleep cycles.
wellness_metric_help.sleep_wake_min: Time spent awake or restless during the night. Brief awakenings are normal; frequent ones may signal poor sleep quality.
wellness_metric_help.sleep_efficiency: Percentage of time in bed actually spent asleep. Above 85% is generally considered good.
wellness_metric_help.sleep_score: Overall sleep quality score out of 100. Factors in duration, sleep stage balance, SpO2, and HRV.
wellness_metric_help.sleep_time_to_fall_asleep_min: How long it took to settle into deep sleep after first falling asleep. Lower is generally better.
wellness_metric_help.sleep_sound_sleep_min: Longest stretch of uninterrupted sleep (LIGHT, DEEP, and REM with no wake events). Approximation of Fitbit's Sound Sleep metric — Fitbit's exact algorithm is proprietary and may use motion data the API does not expose.
wellness_metric_help.sleep_restlessness_min: Brief stirring during the night — short AWAKE segments under 5 minutes. Approximation of Fitbit's Restlessness metric, which also incorporates motion data the API does not expose.
wellness_metric_help.sleep_interruptions_min: Wake events of 5 minutes or longer that you're likely to remember. Card shows total minutes and the count of awakenings.
wellness_metric_help.sleep_full_awakenings: Number of distinct wake events of 5 minutes or longer. Shown alongside Interruptions on the same card.
wellness_metric_help.resting_hr: Heart rate when fully at rest. Lower is generally better — a downward trend over time reflects improving cardiovascular fitness.
wellness_metric_help.avg_heart_rate: Average heart rate across the day from your wearable. Rises with activity, stress, and elevated body temperature; useful for spotting an unusually high or low day at a glance.
wellness_metric_help.spo2_avg: Blood oxygen saturation measured overnight. Healthy range is typically 95–100%. Dips below 90% may indicate sleep apnea.
wellness_metric_help.respiratory_rate: Average breaths per minute during sleep. Normal adult range is 12–20 breaths/min. Elevated values may signal illness or stress.
wellness_metric_help.hrv_daily_rmssd: Heart rate variability — the variation between heartbeats. Higher values indicate better recovery and autonomic nervous system balance.
wellness_metric_help.skin_temp_variation: Nightly skin temperature variation from your personal baseline. Elevated readings can indicate illness or hormonal changes.
wellness_metric_help.vo2_max: Estimated VO₂ Max — the maximum oxygen your body can use during exercise. Fitbit shows this as a range (e.g. 39–43 mL/kg/min). A key indicator of long-term cardiovascular health.
wellness_metric_help.max_hr: Highest heart rate recorded during the day. Useful for tracking workout intensity and your true max effort.
wellness_metric_help.weight_kg: Current body weight from your scale.
wellness_metric_help.body_fat_pct: Percentage of total body weight that is fat tissue. Healthy ranges vary by age and sex.
wellness_metric_help.muscle_mass_kg: Total skeletal muscle mass. Higher values indicate better strength and metabolic health.
wellness_metric_help.bone_mass_kg: Estimated bone mineral content. Stable values are normal; significant drops may warrant discussion with your doctor.
wellness_metric_help.body_water_pct: Total body water as a percentage of weight. Normal range is 45–65% depending on age and sex.
wellness_metric_help.lean_mass_kg: Everything except fat — includes muscle, bone, organs, and water.
wellness_metric_help.fat_mass_kg: Total fat tissue weight. Tracking trends is more useful than individual readings.
wellness_metric_help.visceral_fat: Fat stored around internal organs. Higher levels are linked to increased metabolic and cardiovascular risk.
wellness_metric_help.visceral_fat_index: Indexed rating of visceral fat. Lower is better — a score under 13 is generally considered healthy.
wellness_metric_help.extracellular_water_kg: Water outside cells (blood, lymph, interstitial fluid). Elevated levels may indicate inflammation or fluid retention.
wellness_metric_help.intracellular_water_kg: Water inside cells. Reflects hydration at the cellular level — higher relative to extracellular is generally healthier.
wellness_metric_help.vascular_age: Estimated age of your arteries based on pulse wave velocity. Lower than your actual age indicates healthier blood vessels.
wellness_metric_help.metabolic_age: Your body's metabolic efficiency compared to age norms. Lower than your actual age means your metabolism is performing well.
wellness_metric_help.basal_metabolic_rate: Calories your body burns at complete rest over 24 hours. Influenced by muscle mass, age, and body composition.
wellness_metric_help.nerve_health_score: Monthly nerve health score from your Withings scale. Calculated from daily EDA readings over the month. Above 50 = Normal, below 50 = Low. Final score confirmed at month-end.
wellness_metric_help.eda_feet: Daily electrodermal activity reading from your Withings scale. Measures sweat gland nerve conductance in your feet. These daily readings feed into the monthly Nerve Health Score.
wellness_metric_help.pulse_wave_velocity: Speed of blood pressure pulse along arteries. Lower values indicate more elastic, healthier blood vessels.
wellness_metric_help.ecg_heart_rate: Heart rate measured during ECG recording on your scale. More accurate than optical wrist sensors.
wellness_metric_help.ecg_afib: Atrial fibrillation screening from ECG recording. "Normal" means no irregular rhythm detected during this reading.
wellness_metric_help.body_battery_high: Highest Body Battery level today (0–100). Charges during rest and sleep, drains during activity and stress.
wellness_metric_help.body_battery_low: Lowest Body Battery level today. If it drops below 20, your body may need rest or recovery.
wellness_metric_help.stress_avg: Average stress level from Garmin (0–100). Measured via heart rate variability throughout the day. Lower is calmer.

provider_help.auth0: Auth0 adds custom claims under a namespaced URL like "https://nutritrace.app/roles" — leave the admin claim blank for now and contact your tenant admin to set up a rule that exposes role membership.
provider_help.authelia: Authelia's issuer URL is the root URL where Authelia is served — no path suffix.
provider_help.authentik: Issuer URL is the "OpenID Configuration Issuer" shown on the Provider page in Authentik. Make sure your Application uses an OAuth2/OIDC Provider and you've added the redirect URI shown above to its allowed list.
provider_help.google: Google's issuer URL is fixed. Group/role claims are not available with standard scopes — admin role mapping is hidden for this provider; promote Google users manually after first login.
provider_help.keycloak: Add a "groups" mapper to your client's default scope so the groups claim is included in the ID token.
provider_help.pocket-id: Pocket ID uses passkeys for primary auth — your users won't need a password at the IdP either. Add the redirect URI shown above to the OIDC client in Pocket ID admin.
provider_help.custom: Any OpenID Connect 1.0 compliant provider that supports Authorization Code Flow + PKCE + Discovery should work here.
